name: Superserve

modes.label: Sandbox, pay-as-you-go (allocated vCPU + RAM per second while active)
modes.note: $0.000014/vCPU-s and $0.0000045/GiB-s (effective 2026-06-17 per public billing API). Memory is 'allocated memory, billed per second of active runtime'. Shape is fixed per template: 1-4 vCPU, 256-4096 MiB RAM, 1-8 GiB disk (platform ceiling); new teams capped at 2 vCPU / 2 GiB until support raises it. Paused = no compute. Auto-pause (timeoutSeconds, max 7 d) is off by default and counts active time, not idleness: a forgotten sandbox bills until paused/killed. Basis check 2026-09-28: vCPU 'Per-second billing. Pay only while sandboxes are running.'; memory 'Allocated memory, billed per second of active runtime.' (https://superserve.ai/pricing): 'active runtime' means the running state, not CPU use, so alloc/alloc. Auto-pause 'is a cap on active time, not idle time' and is off by default (https://docs.superserve.ai/sandbox/lifecycle), so auto_stop_idle stays false.

evidence.quote: By default, a sandbox can reach any public IP on the internet.
Lock down sandbox egress to specific CIDRs or domains with allow and deny lists.

plans.name: Pay-as-you-go
plans.note: No fee, no card to start. Per-team active-sandbox limit exists (429 too_many_sandboxes) but its value is unpublished; raise via support. New teams capped at 2 vCPU / 2 GiB per sandbox.

plans.name: Enterprise (on-prem)
plans.note: On-premise deployment and dedicated support; contact sales. Pricing unpublished.

perf_source: benchmarks.json computesdk: cold_start_tti median 316.3 ms (2026-08-07), burst_tti median 516.33 ms at 100 concurrency (2026-09-25), DAX total 94.14 s (2026-09-25; env 8 logical CPUs / 15.7 GiB / x86_64 - larger than the documented 4 vCPU ceiling, so the benchmark account likely had raised limits). No hpc CPU run.
caveats: Per-sandbox shape is fixed per template. Platform ceiling is 10 vCPU / 20 GiB RAM / 64 GiB disk (OpenAPI schema + controlplane absoluteMax* constants; the docs build-spec table still shows the older 4 vCPU / 4096 MiB / 8192 MiB). New teams are capped at 2 vCPU / 2 GiB / 8 GiB disk and 10 templates; larger shapes need an email to support. A 4 vCPU / 8 GiB workload is feasible only after support raises the cap.

Storage $0.000108/GiB-h (= $0.07884/GiB-month at 730 h) is on the pricing page ('Paused sandboxes are billed only for storage'), but the public billing API (effective 2026-06-17) marks storage billable:false and the usage-series docs say storage 'remains tracked-only and is excluded' from billed totals. Card uses the published list price; today's invoices appear to charge $0 for storage/snapshots. Whether running-sandbox disk is also metered as storage is not stated.
Paused sandboxes are kept forever by default (autoDeleteSeconds optional, max 30 days); with storage unbilled they currently cost nothing.
Auto-pause is opt-in and based on active time, not idleness: an idle but running sandbox bills full allocated vCPU+RAM.

Free credit: pricing page only says 'Start for free, no credit card'. Vendor source code (superserve-ai/sandbox PR #454, merged 2026-09-25) shows a $5 signup trial grant plus a $95 activation bonus on Stripe checkout (card added), one redemption per user; encoded as one_time_credit 100 (not on the pricing page).
Egress/ingress not metered in the public rate card (only vcpu, memory_gib, storage_gib meters exist); not stated as free, so null.
Billing granularity per second; minimum billed time not published. Regions not documented (API is cell-based).
Rates are identical to E2B's list rates.

Other per-team limits: 100 snapshots per team, 20 per sandbox, 4 in flight (docs, raisable via support); API request rate 50 req/s with burst 150 per team (vendor source ratelimit.go, not documented).

Vendor source (migration 20260929000001_prospective_storage_billing) adds a per-team storage-billing activation cutoff; the public billing API still marks storage billable:false, so the listed $0.000108/GiB-h storage may start being invoiced team by team.

fleet.notes: Official error docs explicitly enforce per-team active sandbox count (429 too_many_sandboxes) and say pause/delete or contact support. Numeric default and higher limits unpublished; no guaranteed 10/50/300/1,000 fleet or review SLA.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: Set `timeoutSeconds` to auto-pause a sandbox after it has been active for that long. Pausing checkpoints its state and stops compute billing, so a sandbox you forget about won't keep running and billing.
snapshot_auto.note: Opt-in (off by default); trigger is a cap on active time, not idleness ('It's a cap on active time, not idle time'). Memory included: 'Resume restores full memory and filesystem.' Next commands.run()/file op/connect() auto-resumes. No idle-based pause.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: A snapshot saves a sandbox's memory and disk at a point in time. Sandboxes you create from a snapshot are called forks. A fork starts exactly where the snapshot left off, with its files, installed packages and running processes in place.
snapshot_on_demand.note: Memory included; of an active (paused <1 s for capture) or paused sandbox; any number of new sandboxes boot from it via from_snapshot; snapshots outlive the source sandbox. Limits: 100 per team, 20 per sandbox. Plus manual pause() = full VM checkpoint of the same sandbox.

harness_api.quote: Open the sandbox in the [console](https://console.superserve.ai?utm_source=docs\&utm_medium=link), launch the terminal, and run `claude`.
harness_api.note: Agents are provided as templates (superserve/claude-code; guides for Codex, OpenCode, Kilocode, OpenClaw, Hermes) and run via terminal/exec (exec, SSE stream, WebSocket, interactive sessions). The Claude Managed Agents and Cursor Self-Hosted Machines integrations use Anthropic's/Cursor's own session APIs with Superserve only as the execution sandbox. No first-party Superserve API to start an agent with a prompt or manage its conversations.

egress_allowlist.quote: `allowOut` / `allow_out` accepts a mix of CIDRs and domain patterns. Combine it with `denyOut: ["0.0.0.0/0"]` to build a strict allowlist - deny everything, then add exceptions.
egress_allowlist.note: Per sandbox; default allows all public internet; private/link-local/loopback always blocked; denyOut takes IPs/CIDRs only; domain rules matched on the connection; updatable live on an active sandbox; forks inherit rules. Platform-recorded network log of HTTP/HTTPS (80/443) connections.

egress_http_rules.note: Rule format is only allowOut (IPs/CIDRs/domains) and denyOut (IPs/CIDRs); no method/path/header rules. Only HTTP-level control is secret injection scoped per host. Network log records method/path/status (observability, not policy).

ingress_rules.quote:
Every published port stores its own `public` or `private` access mode. Changing
the sandbox default does not rewrite existing ports, so public and private ports
can coexist in one sandbox.
ingress_rules.note: Strict publication: only explicitly published ports are reachable (others 404); per-port public vs private; private ports need a minted token (header) scoped to sandbox+port, rotatable per port. No IP allowlist; no raw TCP; legacy_public mode only for old sandboxes.

guest_firewall.note: Firecracker microVM with its own kernel and root (templates run as root / sudo users; 'every Superserve sandbox is a full Firecracker microVM, FUSE works inside', storage/archil). iptables/nftables inside not documented.

secret_proxy.quote: Code running inside the sandbox never sees the real value. It sees a **stand-in token**, and Superserve swaps that token for your real credential as each request leaves the sandbox — only on requests to the hosts you allow.
secret_proxy.note: Provider shortcuts (Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, OpenRouter, GitHub, GitLab, Vercel, Cloudflare, Stripe, Notion, Resend...) plus custom secrets with auth type bearer / api-key header / basic / custom header templates for any hosts (secrets/create). Host-scoped; attach/detach/rotate live; per-secret audit log of every request. HTTP(S) header injection only; databases/SSH not covered (DATABASE_URL shown as plain env var).

volume_attach.note: No first-party volume: create-sandbox schema has no volume/mount field and the docs never mention volumes. Storage docs are guides for third-party FUSE mounts inside the VM: Archil elastic disks, Mesa versioned filesystems, S3/GCS/R2 buckets (mountpoint-s3/gcsfuse/rclone style). Disk per sandbox is fixed by template (platform ceiling 8 GiB in docs).

volume_shared.quote: Mount an Archil **disk** inside a Superserve sandbox to give it a fast workspace whose data persists across runs, survives the sandbox, and can be mounted by several sandboxes at once with `--shared`.
volume_shared.note: Not first-party: shared read-write filesystems only via the third-party Archil service (own account/billing) or user-mounted buckets, documented as integration guides.

nested_virt.note: Not documented anywhere (no /dev/kvm, nested virtualization, or 'run VMs inside your sandbox' mention across docs/build-spec/OpenAPI). Firecracker microVMs do not expose hardware virtualization extensions to the guest by default, so nested KVM is not available; derived.

browser.quote: Virtual machines for long-horizon agents. Durable Firecracker VMs that pause indefinitely, resume instantly, and run as long as your agents need.
browser.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Superserve is a generic Firecracker sandbox/VM runtime for code execution — the homepage lists running 'AI-generated code, browsers, or system tasks' as a use case a customer can build, but there is no managed/preinstalled browser, browser template, or browser-control API documented anywhere in docs.superserve.ai.

anti_bot.quote: Superserve — Virtual machines for long-horizon agents.
anti_bot.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. No stealth/fingerprinting features are mentioned anywhere in the docs; the product is generic sandbox infrastructure, not a browser-automation/anti-bot product.

captcha_solving.quote: Superserve — Virtual machines for long-horizon agents.
captcha_solving.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. No CAPTCHA-solving feature is mentioned anywhere in the docs; the product is generic sandbox/VM infrastructure, not a browser/scraping product.

egress_ip_type.quote: By default, a sandbox can reach any public IP on the internet. The platform always blocks egress to private, link-local, and loopback ranges regardless of your allow rules.
egress_ip_type.note: derived: sandboxes run as Firecracker microVMs on cloud infrastructure (Google Cloud Platform is a listed subprocessor in the Vanta trust center); no residential/mobile proxy product is offered or mentioned, so outbound traffic uses standard cloud/datacenter IPs.

ssh.quote: Reconnect to a sandbox you created earlier using its ID, and list sandboxes on your team.
ssh.note: not offered: access to a sandbox is exclusively via the SDK/API (commands.run/spawn, exec REST/SSE/WebSocket, files API). SSH is never mentioned in the docs, quickstart, SDK reference, or OpenAPI spec — there is no SSH endpoint or key-injection mechanism documented.

fork_running.quote: The sandbox must be active or paused. A running sandbox is paused for the capture: under a second for the first memory snapshot of a sandbox, longer when all of memory has to be written.
fork_running.note: Forking (via a snapshot + from_snapshot) briefly pauses a running sandbox to take the memory+disk snapshot before it resumes, so it is not cloned while continuously running.

wake_on_request.quote: Returns the sandbox with a fresh access token. If the sandbox is paused, it is resumed first. Idempotent — calling it on an active sandbox just returns a new token.
wake_on_request.note: Confirmed broadly: 'sandbox_exec and the file tools transparently resume a paused sandbox, so agents never need to call sandbox_resume first' and 'A paused sandbox wakes on its own before the session opens' (commands/sessions.md) — any exec/file/connect call auto-resumes a paused sandbox.

live_resize.note: The homepage markets 'Elastic resource allocation — Let your agents request CPU/memory resources on the fly from within the box', but the documented PATCH /sandboxes/{id} endpoint (the only way to modify a running sandbox) does not include a vcpu/memory field, and no separate resize endpoint exists in the OpenAPI spec; per-sandbox vCPU/RAM is fixed by the template at creation.

own_agent_api.quote: Superserve — Virtual machines for long-horizon agents.
own_agent_api.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Superserve provides only sandbox/VM execution infrastructure; coding/browser/research agents are third-party (Claude Code, Codex, Claude Managed Agents, Cursor Cloud Agents, LangChain, OpenAI Agents SDK, Agno) run by the customer inside the sandbox — there is no first-party Superserve agent or API to drive one.

static_egress_ip.quote: By default, a sandbox can reach any public IP on the internet.
static_egress_ip.note: No fixed/static outbound IP, elastic IP, or NAT-gateway feature is documented anywhere; network controls only cover allow/deny rules by CIDR/domain, not a stable egress address. Matches card's network.ipv4_available: false (no public IPv4 either).

sso.quote: Get team management state ... Returns the caller-visible team members, role assignments, and capability flags used by customer-facing member management UI.
sso.note: Team membership is managed by email invite plus role assignment; no SAML/OIDC/SSO endpoint, field, or mention exists anywhere in the RBAC API, docs, pricing, or enterprise page (enterprise plan only advertises 'on-premise deployment and dedicated support').

eu_data_residency.quote: Superserve provides sandbox infrastructure to run code in isolated cloud environments powered by Firecracker MicroVMs.
eu_data_residency.note: No region-selection field exists on sandbox/template creation and no EU/Europe region is mentioned anywhere in the docs; the card's own researched regions list is ["us"] only (API described as cell-based with no documented region parameter).

max_session_h.note: A sandbox stays active until paused/deleted or an opt-in timeout_seconds cap (off by default, max 7 days for the auto-pause trigger) is set; there is no mandatory maximum runtime after which the platform force-stops a sandbox.

persistent_disk.quote: Pausing checkpoints its state and stops compute billing... Resume restores full memory and filesystem.
persistent_disk.note: pause()/resume() is a full VM checkpoint (memory+processes+filesystem) that survives a stop; files are not lost. Card's persistent_disk:false contradicts its own pause_resume:true and snapshot fields. Correct to true, with the caveat that it's opt-in checkpoint/pause-resume (and named snapshots/forks), not a permanently-attached separate disk (no volume_attach).

desktop.quote: system: "You are a coding assistant with a Linux sandbox."
desktop.note: Superserve is a headless Firecracker microVM sandbox for code exec/agents (exec, files, templates from OCI images); no VNC/RDP/streamed GUI desktop is offered or documented anywhere in the docs.

computer_use.note: The only 'screenshot' reference is Cloud Agent artifact uploads (e.g. browser-driven CI runs), not a first-party API to drive a desktop via screenshots+clicks. No computer-use / desktop-control API is documented; consistent with desktop:false (no GUI to control).

auto_stop_idle.quote: It's a cap on active time, not idle time. Running work doesn't reset it, so a task still going when the window elapses is paused mid-run.
auto_stop_idle.note: Auto-pause (timeoutSeconds) is opt-in and keyed to cumulative active seconds, not idleness; an idle-but-running sandbox is not detected/stopped. No separate idle-detection feature exists.

public_ipv4.quote: Preview URLs route a hostname such as `https://3000-{sandbox-id}.sandbox.superserve.ai` to a process listening inside your sandbox.
public_ipv4.note: Inbound access is exclusively via shared-hostname HTTPS preview URLs, not a per-sandbox public IPv4 address; no public IPv4 is offered or mentioned anywhere in networking docs.

gpu.note: The public billing API and pricing page only meter vCPU/RAM/storage; templates/build-spec require a linux/amd64 OCI base image with no GPU option; no GPU instance type, pricing, or docs exist anywhere in the product.

windows.note: Sandboxes are built exclusively from Linux OCI base images (linux/amd64); no Windows base image or Windows machine type is offered.

macos.note: Same evidence as windows: Firecracker microVM sandboxes only run linux/amd64 OCI images; macOS is only referenced as an allowed *client/controller* OS for reaching Superserve (e.g. Cursor guide), never as a sandboxed machine type.

arm64.note: Build-spec explicitly restricts templates to linux/amd64; no arm64 base image or machine type is documented anywhere.

open_source.quote: Open Core Ventures Source Available License (OCVSAL) version 1.0 ... Using software and associated documentation files (the "Software") in production requires a valid commercial agreement from the copyright holder.
open_source.note: The core sandbox repo (superserve-ai/sandbox, source of the OpenAPI spec) is source-available, not OSI open source; production use needs a paid commercial agreement. Other public superserve-ai repos (langchain-superserve, guides) are example/integration code, not the core product.

private_network.quote: By default, a sandbox can reach any public IP on the internet. The platform always blocks egress to private, link-local, and loopback ranges regardless of your allow rules.
private_network.note: Networking docs cover only an egress allow/deny-list to public destinations and per-port preview access; there is no VPC/private-network peering or sandbox-to-sandbox private network feature documented; private/link-local ranges are always blocked, not offered as a reachable private network.

usage_api.quote: A public billing API (effective 2026-06-17) with meter data for vcpu, memory_gib, storage_gib tracked per sandbox per team. Rate card shows $0.000014/vCPU-s and $0.0000045/GiB-s, allowing cost calculation from usage.
usage_api.note: granularity: per-sandbox; cost: yes; The documented endpoint retrieves billing usage chart buckets scoped to team/sandbox. The public pricing API and the usage metrics endpoint are both explicitly listed in the card sources and documented in Superserve's billing API reference.

locations_quote: Regions not documented (API is cell-based). Sandbox IDs include a region-tag prefix (e.g., sb-use-uuid) but available regions are not listed in pricing, docs, or API reference.
